newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes lower led by major issues.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes lower led by major issues.

text.p: The Czech PX50 index shrugged off a strong performance from SPT Telecom on Monday closing 0.4 percent lower to 606.6 led by major issues CEZ, Komercni Banka and Ceska Sporitelna.
CEZ was the day's biggest loser, dropping 27 crowns, 2.2 percent, to 1,178 while Komercni fell back from early gains to close down 25 crowns, 0.9 percent, to 2,725.
Dealers say both companies have been pushed lower by worse than expected 1996 profit figures but add that volumes have been low and that prices have been mainly driven by local investors.
"I haven't seen significant orders from foreigners. It is, I think, local market makers doing this (pushing CEZ and Komercni down)," said Tomas Vejvoda of CS First Boston.

On Monday, CEZ said that preliminary 1996 gross profits had fallen to 13.7 billion crowns from 14.78 billion in 1995 while after bourse trading closed on Friday, Komercni said that its net 1996 profit, according to international accounting standards, had risen to a disappointing 5.24 billion crowns from 5.11 in 1995.
Sporitelna dropped nine crowns, 2.7 percent, to 318.

SPT Telecom's 60 crown, 1.5 percent, rise to 3,840 was not strong enough to overcome the combined downward pressure from the above three issues which taken together account for more than 30 percent of the PX50's capitalisation.
